advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the `self._client.fields()` discovery call through `_call_logged`/`_with_connection_retry` so it gets the same connection-retry and WARNING logging as every other transport network call.
evidence: transport.py:715-718: `self._epic_link_field_id = next((f.get("id") for f in lister() if f.get("name") == "Epic Link"), None,)` — `lister()` is called directly, not through `_call_logged`

transport.py:698 `issue = _call_logged("set_parent", remote_id, lambda: self._client.issue(remote_id))` and :734 `_call_logged("set_parent", remote_id, lambda: issue.update(fields=body))` show every other network op in this method routes through the choke point
transport.py:178-205 `_call_logged` docstring: 'the single choke point every member routes through' and 'run fn() through _with_connection_retry'
transport.py:25-29 module docstring documents connection-level faults are retried up to 2 times — the fields() call is exempted from this policy
advisory.finding: The Epic Link field-discovery call `lister()` (self._client.fields()) is not wrapped in `_call_logged`/`_with_connection_retry`, unlike every other network call in the transport, so a transient ConnectionError/Timeout during `GET /rest/api/2/field` gets no connection-level retry and no choke-point WARNING log.
scenarios: A reparent-heavy pass where the first set_parent's field discovery hits a transient connection blip: the whole pass's parent writes fail with no retry, whereas the equivalent blip on issue.update would be retried
Operators lose the WARNING signal for a fields() failure that the module deliberately emits at the choke point for every other member
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the discovery in the choke point, e.g. `field_list = _call_logged("set_parent", remote_id, lambda: lister())` then compute the id from `field_list`, so a transient fault is retried and logged consistently.

ABSENCE: no test constructs _FakeClient(subtask=False, epic_link_name=None), calls set_parent twice, and asserts field_calls == 1
advisory.finding: The negative-cache behavior — a fieldless instance is cached (as None) and NOT re-probed on subsequent set_parent calls — is untested. The transport deliberately distinguishes `_MISSING` from `None` (transport.py:239-241, 707-718) so a fieldless instance is looked up once; but no unit test calls set_parent twice on a client whose fields() has no 'Epic Link' and asserts field_calls stays at 1. A regression that only cached non-None results (re-probing a fieldless instance on every write) would keep every existing test green.
scenarios: An instance without Jira Software (no 'Epic Link' field) undergoes a reparent-heavy outbound pass: every set_parent on a non-sub-task would re-issue GET /rest/api/2/field if the None result were not cached — the exact REST-cost regression the _MISSING/None distinction exists to prevent (ticket b586).
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: `client = _FakeClient(subtask=False, epic_link_name=None); t = _transport(client);` then call set_parent twice (each expecting NotImplementedError) and `assert client.field_calls == 1`.
